measures.title: AI Gigafactories deadline extended for Lot 1
measures.summary: The deadline for Lot 1 tenders was extended to 4 February 2027 so member states can complete budget procedures; Lot 2 still closes on 3 December 2026.
measures.source_title: EuroHPC JU: AI Gigafactories call for tenders

measures.title: A rating scheme and label for data centres adopted
measures.summary: The Commission adopted a delegated regulation setting up a common EU rating scheme for data centres. Its label would show each data centre's name, operator and location. A delegated regulation enters into force only if the Parliament and Council do not object.

measures.actor: German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs
measures.title: Germany publishes its data-centre register
measures.summary: Germany's energy-efficiency register for data centres was published, giving official data on data centres in Germany for the first time. The Federal Environment Agency says the coverage of published data centres is highly incomplete.

measures.title: Commission's enforcement powers for general-purpose AI apply
measures.summary: From 2 August 2026, the Commission can enforce the obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models, including with fines. Models already on the market before 2 August 2025 must comply by 2 August 2027.
measures.source_title: Commission: guidelines for providers of general-purpose AI models

measures.actor: European Commission and EuroHPC Joint Undertaking
measures.title: Call for tenders for up to seven AI Gigafactories
measures.summary: The EU opened a call for tenders for up to seven AI Gigafactories, with up to EUR 10 billion of EU and national funding expected to unlock at least EUR 20 billion of private investment. Selection is expected in early 2027.

measures.title: Data centres used 23% of Ireland's metered electricity in 2025
measures.summary: The CSO reported that data centres used 7,663 GWh of electricity in 2025, 23% of all metered electricity, up from 5% in 2015. The figures come from meter data.
measures.source_title: CSO: Data Centres Metered Electricity Consumption 2025

measures.title: Six more AI Factories selected: 19 across 16 member states
measures.summary: Six further AI Factories were selected, bringing the network to 19 AI Factories across 16 member states, complemented by 13 smaller AI Factory Antennas announced on 13 October 2025.
measures.source_title: Commission: EU announces AI Factories Antennas

measures.title: AI Act rules for general-purpose AI models start to apply
measures.summary: Providers of general-purpose AI models must meet transparency and copyright obligations. Models trained with more than 10^25 floating-point operations are presumed to carry systemic risk, and their providers must notify the Commission and assess and mitigate those risks. The Commission says this threshold is under review.

measures.title: General-Purpose AI Code of Practice received
measures.summary: The Commission received the final General-Purpose AI Code of Practice from independent experts: a voluntary tool explaining how providers can meet their AI Act obligations, including safety and security for models with systemic risk.
measures.source_title: Commission: guidelines for providers of general-purpose AI models

measures.title: InvestAI announced: EUR 20 billion for AI Gigafactories
measures.summary: Commission President von der Leyen announced that EUR 20 billion would be mobilised to finance several AI Gigafactories across the EU.

measures.title: Data centres of 500 kW or more must report their energy use
measures.summary: A delegated regulation under the Energy Efficiency Directive requires operators of data centres with an installed IT power demand of at least 500 kW to report energy and water indicators every year to a European database. The data is published only in aggregated form.

profile.question: public_list
profile.detail: The European database publishes data centre figures only in aggregated form, by member state and EU-wide, not facility by facility. A rating scheme adopted in September 2026 would put each data centre's name, operator and location on a label, once it is in force.

profile.question: energy_reporting
profile.detail: Operators of data centres with an installed IT power demand of at least 500 kW must report energy and water indicators every year to the European database.
profile.source_title: Commission: energy performance of data centres

profile.question: official_figures
profile.detail: The Commission publishes an online dashboard of the aggregated data, and reports analysing it (July 2025, and September 2026). Figures are aggregated, not per data centre.
profile.source_title: Commission: energy performance of data centres

profile.question: public_list
profile.detail: Germany published its data-centre register on 14 August 2026, but the Federal Environment Agency says the coverage of published data centres is highly incomplete.

profile.question: energy_reporting
profile.detail: Under the Energy Efficiency Act (EnEfG), data centre operators report each year to the national register, which passes the data to the European database.
profile.source_title: Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs: data-centre register

profile.question: official_figures
profile.detail: The Central Statistics Office publishes data centres' metered electricity use: 7,663 GWh in 2025, 23% of all metered electricity, from meter data.
profile.source_title: CSO: Data Centres Metered Electricity Consumption 2025

incidents.title: SyRI welfare fraud-detection system halted by court
incidents.summary: The District Court of The Hague ruled the SyRI legislation (Systeem Risico Indicatie) unlawful for breaching Article 8 ECHR: the opaque, inter-agency data-linkage risk model targeted low-income neighbourhoods and lacked sufficient safeguards, with a risk of discrimination by socio-economic and migration background. The system was halted.
incidents.notes: Judgment: District Court of The Hague, ECLI:NL:RBDHA:2020:865 (English ECLI:NL:RBDHA:2020:1878).

incidents.title: Clearview AI — untargeted scraping of facial images in France
incidents.summary: CNIL order (MED-2021-134, 26 November 2021, made public 6 December 2021) finding Clearview AI unlawfully collected and processed facial images of people in France without a legal basis to build a facial-recognition database sold to law enforcement.
incidents.notes: Order of 26 November 2021, made public 6 December 2021.

incidents.title: ChatGPT data breach exposing users' conversations and payment data
incidents.summary: On 20 March 2023 a ChatGPT bug exposed other users' chat histories and partial payment details; the breach was cited by the Garante in its 31 March 2023 action against OpenAI, alongside the absence of a legal basis for training-data collection and of age verification.
incidents.source_title: Garante, 31 Mar 2023: Artificial intelligence: stop to ChatGPT by the Italian SA
incidents.notes: Breach cited by the Garante in its 31 March 2023 action against OpenAI.

incidents.title: Grok sexualised deepfakes disseminated on X
incidents.summary: The Commission found the risks of Grok's functionalities deployed into X "seem to have materialised", with manipulated sexually explicit images — including content that may amount to child sexual abuse material — disseminated in the EU, exposing citizens to serious harm.

incidents.title: Dutch childcare benefits scandal (Toeslagenaffaire) — nationality-based risk profiling
incidents.summary: The parliamentary inquiry report 'Ongekend onrecht' (17 December 2020) found the Tax Administration's childcare-benefit fraud approach used a risk model that included a self-learning algorithm with (dual) nationality as an indicator. Around 26,000 families were wrongly accused of fraud and faced full recovery of benefits; the approach ran from about 2005 to 2019, and the cabinet resigned on 15 January 2021.
incidents.source_title: Tweede Kamer, Kamerstukken II 2020/21, 35 510, nr. 2 — 'Ongekend onrecht'
incidents.notes: Risk profiling ran about 2005–2019; around 26,000 families wrongly accused; cabinet resigned 15 January 2021.

incidents.title: Clearview AI — untargeted scraping of facial images including Greek residents
incidents.summary: A complaint by Homo Digitalis on behalf of a Greek resident (right of access) led the Hellenic Data Protection Authority to find that Clearview AI had collected facial images of Greek residents without a legal basis to build a facial-recognition database.
incidents.notes: Dated to the complaint of 26 May 2021 (G/IN/3458/26-05-2021); the Authority's decision followed on 13 July 2022.

incidents.title: Swedish Police Authority's unlawful use of Clearview AI facial recognition
incidents.summary: The Swedish Police Authority used Clearview AI's facial-recognition app from autumn 2019 to 3 March 2020 without a lawful basis, in breach of the Criminal Data Act; the Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection (IMY) found the use unlawful.
incidents.source_title: Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection (IMY), 11 Feb 2021
incidents.notes: Dated to 3 March 2020, the last day of the documented use period; IMY decision DI-2020-2719 of 10 February 2021.

responses.actor: Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés (CNIL)
responses.summary: CNIL's restricted committee imposed the then-maximum GDPR fine of €20m on Clearview AI for unlawful biometric processing, failure to honour access/erasure rights and non-cooperation, ordered it to stop collecting French residents' data and delete what it held within two months, under a €100,000/day penalty. Announced 20 October 2022.
responses.notes: Fine announced 20 October 2022; €100,000/day penalty for non-compliance. The CNIL's own press-release page for the sanction is no longer published (named decisions are delisted after the publicity period), so the decision text is linked via Légifrance.

responses.summary: The Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens fined the Minister of Finance/Tax Administration €3.7m for the Fraude Signalering Voorziening (FSV), a blacklist holding fraud signals on over 270,000 people (2013–2020) with no legal basis, inaccurate/outdated data, excessive retention and inadequate security. Decision 7 April 2022, published 12 April 2022.
responses.source_title: Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens, 12 Apr 2022: Boete Belastingdienst voor zwarte lijst FSV
responses.notes: Decision of 7 April 2022, published 12 April 2022. No single incident row: the FSV blacklist ran 2013–2020 and no verified incident date was established. The full fine decision is linked under 'Publicaties' on the AP page.

responses.actor: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali
responses.summary: The Garante imposed an urgent temporary limitation on Luka Inc.'s processing of Italian users' data via the Replika AI companion chatbot, finding concrete risks to minors (sexually inappropriate replies, no age verification) and no valid legal basis for processing children's data.
responses.source_title: Garante, 3 Feb 2023: Artificial intelligence: italian SA clamps down on 'Replika' chatbot
responses.notes: Urgent temporary limitation on Luka Inc.'s processing of Italian users' data via Replika.

responses.actor: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali
responses.summary: The Garante ordered an immediate temporary limitation on OpenAI's processing of Italians' personal data via ChatGPT (provision of 30 March 2023, announced 31 March), citing no legal basis for mass training-data collection, no user information, inaccurate outputs and no age verification; the Garante set conditions on 12 April 2023 for lifting the limitation; service resumed 28 April 2023.
responses.source_title: Garante, 31 Mar 2023: Artificial intelligence: stop to ChatGPT by the Italian SA
responses.notes: Provision of 30 March 2023, announced 31 March; the Garante set conditions on 12 April 2023 for lifting the limitation (OpenAI to comply by 30 April); service resumed 28 April 2023.

responses.summary: The Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens imposed a €30.5m fine on Clearview AI (decision 16 May 2024, announced 3 September 2024) for its illegal facial-recognition database of 30bn+ photos including Dutch citizens, plus an order subject to a penalty of up to €5.1m for continued non-compliance; it is also examining personal liability of directors.
responses.notes: Decision of 16 May 2024, announced 3 September 2024. Not linked to FR-I-01: that incident is the French CNIL finding; the Dutch fine concerns Clearview's database including Dutch citizens.

responses.summary: Report of the EDPB ChatGPT Taskforce (established 13 April 2023) setting out preliminary views on lawfulness, fairness, accuracy, transparency and data-subject rights for ChatGPT, including that web-scraped training data poses fundamental-rights risks and that compliance responsibility cannot be transferred to data subjects.
responses.source_title: European Data Protection Board, ChatGPT Taskforce report

responses.summary: The DPC concluded High Court proceedings (brought 8 August 2024 under s.134 Data Protection Act 2018) after X agreed permanently to adhere to its undertaking on processing EU/EEA users' public posts to train Grok; the DPC had warned of risks to fundamental rights, and simultaneously asked the EDPB for the Art. 64(2) opinion that became Opinion 28/2024.
responses.notes: High Court proceedings brought 8 August 2024 under s.134 Data Protection Act 2018. Not linked to EU-I-01: these proceedings concerned Grok training, not the 2026 deepfakes.

responses.actor: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali
responses.summary: The Garante ordered an urgent, immediate limitation on Hangzhou and Beijing DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence's processing of Italian users' data and opened an investigation, after the companies' reply to its 28 January information request was judged "completely insufficient" and they claimed EU law did not apply to them; the order also cited storage of data in China without GDPR safeguards.
responses.source_title: Garante, 30 Jan 2025: Artificial Intelligence: The Italian Data Protection Authority blocks DeepSeek
responses.notes: Urgent limitation on Hangzhou and Beijing DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence; investigation opened.

responses.summary: The Commission opened new formal DSA proceedings against X and extended its December 2023 proceedings, to assess whether X diligently assessed and mitigated systemic risks from deploying Grok into X (including illegal content, gender-based violence and harm to physical/mental well-being) and filed the required ad hoc risk assessment; suspected infringements of DSA Arts. 34, 35 and 42.
responses.notes: Formal DSA proceedings opened; suspected infringements of DSA Arts. 34, 35 and 42. Binding 'no': proceedings are an investigation, not a final decision.

responses.summary: The Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens fined the Belastingdienst (Tax Administration) €2.75m for unlawful and discriminatory processing of (dual) nationality in childcare-benefit risk profiling under the Toeslagenaffaire, finding the risk model — including a self-learning algorithm using nationality as an indicator — breached the GDPR.
responses.source_title: Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens, 7 Dec 2021: Boete Belastingdienst kinderopvangtoeslag

responses.summary: The DPC announced a statutory inquiry under section 110 of the Data Protection Act 2018 into X Internet Unlimited Company (XIUC), examining the lawfulness and transparency of using EU/EEA users' public posts on X to train Grok large language models.

The DPC opened a large-scale statutory inquiry under section 110 of the Data Protection Act 2018 into X Internet Unlimited Company (XIUC) over the creation and publication on X of potentially harmful, non-consensual intimate and/or sexualised images — including images of children — using Grok's generative AI functionality; the inquiry examines GDPR Articles 5, 6, 25 and 35.
responses.notes: Notified to XIUC on 16 February 2026; linked to EU-I-01 (Grok deepfakes, 26 Jan 2026).

responses.actor: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali
responses.summary: The Garante fined Character Technologies, Inc. €158,000 (Decision No. 487 of 3 July 2026, announced 9 July 2026) over its Character.AI chatbot: inadequate transparency about LLM pre-training use of users' data, insufficient age verification and safeguards for minors, a late data protection impact assessment and a late appointment of an EU representative; the decision ordered compliance within 120 days.

responses.actor: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali
responses.summary: The Garante fined Luka Inc. €5m (decision of 10 April 2025, announced 19 May 2025) over the Replika AI companion chatbot, finding no legal basis for processing, an inadequate privacy policy and no age verification, in breach of GDPR Articles 5.1(a), 6, 12, 13, 5.1(c), 24 and 25.1; Luka Inc. opposed the fine in court (opposition filed 1 July 2025; no judgment on record as of August 2026).
responses.source_title: European Data Protection Board, 21 May 2025: Italian SA fines company behind Replika
responses.notes: The €5m figure is from the EDPB summary — the amount is blacked out in the Garante's published decision. Closes the same Replika case as IT-R-01 (Feb 2023 temporary limitation).

responses.summary: The Hellenic Data Protection Authority fined Clearview AI €20m (Decision 35/2022 of 13 July 2022) for unlawfully collecting and processing facial images of Greek residents without a legal basis; it also banned the collection and processing of Greek residents' data and ordered erasure of data already held.
responses.notes: Complaint G/IN/3458/26-05-2021 by Homo Digitalis on behalf of a Greek resident (right of access).

responses.summary: IMY fined the Swedish Police Authority SEK 2,500,000 (about €250,000) for unlawfully using Clearview AI's facial-recognition app from autumn 2019 to 3 March 2020, in breach of the Criminal Data Act; it also ordered staff training, informing data subjects and erasure of the data.
responses.source_title: Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection (IMY), decision DI-2020-2719
responses.notes: Decision DI-2020-2719 of 10 February 2021, announced 11 February 2021.

instruments.title: General Data Protection Regulation — Regulation (EU) 2016/679
instruments.summary: The EU's general data-protection law, published in the OJ on 4 May 2016 and applicable from 25 May 2018; Arts. 5, 6, 9, 22 and 35 are the main GDPR hooks used against AI training, profiling and automated decision-making.

instruments.title: Digital Services Act — Regulation (EU) 2022/2065
instruments.summary: Sets due-diligence, content-moderation and systemic-risk duties for online intermediaries and very large online platforms; published in the OJ on 27 October 2022, applicable from 17 February 2024. It is the legal basis for the Commission's DSA proceedings against X/Grok.

instruments.title: European AI Office established — Commission Decision C/2024/1459
instruments.summary: Establishes the European AI Office within DG CNECT to implement and enforce the AI Act, especially the rules for general-purpose AI models. Decision of 24 January 2024, published in the OJ on 14 February 2024, in force 21 February 2024.
instruments.notes: Decision of 24 January 2024, published in the OJ on 14 February 2024.

instruments.title: EU AI Act — Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
instruments.summary: The world's first comprehensive AI law: risk-based rules for AI systems, prohibitions, high-risk obligations, GPAI duties and transparency duties. Adopted 13 June 2024, published in the OJ on 12 July 2024, in force 1 August 2024.
instruments.next_milestone: 2 Dec 2027: high-risk duties begin (Annex III stand-alone systems)
instruments.notes: Adopted 13 June 2024.

instruments.title: EDPB Opinion 28/2024 on AI models and personal data
instruments.summary: EDPB opinion (requested by the Irish DPC) on when an AI model trained on personal data can be considered anonymous, when legitimate interest is a lawful basis for training/deployment, and the consequences of unlawful training data.
instruments.notes: Requested by the Irish DPC.

instruments.title: Commission Guidelines on prohibited AI practices (Art. 5 AI Act)
instruments.summary: Non-binding Commission guidelines interpreting the eight prohibited AI practices (manipulation, exploitation of vulnerabilities, social scoring, crime-risk prediction, untargeted facial scraping, emotion recognition, biometric categorisation, real-time remote biometric identification). The prohibitions applied from 2 February 2025.
instruments.source_title: European Commission, Guidelines on prohibited AI practices (C(2025) 884 final, published 4 Feb 2025; formally adopted as C(2025) 5052 final, 29 Jul 2025)
instruments.notes: The prohibitions applied from 2 February 2025. Content approved 4 Feb 2025 as C(2025) 884 final; formally adopted 29 Jul 2025 as C(2025) 5052 final.

instruments.title: General-Purpose AI Code of Practice
instruments.summary: Voluntary code drawn up by 13 independent experts with ~1,000 stakeholders, in three chapters (Transparency, Copyright, Safety and Security), to help GPAI providers demonstrate compliance with Arts. 53 and 55 AI Act. Confirmed by the Commission and AI Board as an adequate voluntary compliance tool.
instruments.notes: Drawn up by 13 independent experts with ~1,000 stakeholders; three chapters (Transparency, Copyright, Safety and Security).

instruments.title: Digital Omnibus on AI — Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
instruments.summary: Amends the AI Act to simplify implementation: postpones high-risk application dates (2 Dec 2027 for stand-alone Annex III systems; 2 Aug 2028 for Annex I product-embedded systems), narrows some duties, and adds two new prohibited practices (Art. 5(1)(ba)–(bb)): AI systems generating non-consensual intimate material and child sexual abuse material, applicable from 2 Dec 2026. Published in the OJ 24 July 2026, in force 27 July 2026.
instruments.next_milestone: 2 Dec 2026: new Art. 5 prohibitions (ba)–(bb) apply; 2 Dec 2027: high-risk duties begin (Annex III stand-alone systems); 2 Aug 2028: Annex I product-embedded systems
instruments.notes: Published in the OJ 24 July 2026.

instruments.title: France — National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: Launched March 2018 following the Villani report; €1,527m public funding for 2018–2022 across research, higher education, public transformation, economy and defence/security, with an acceleration phase announced November 2021 for 2022–2025.
instruments.source_title: Ministère de l'Économie, Stratégie nationale pour l'IA, 2e phase — dossier de presse, 8 Nov 2021
instruments.notes: Following the Villani report; €1,527m public funding for 2018–2022; acceleration phase announced November 2021 for 2022–2025.

instruments.title: Germany — AI Strategy of the Federal Government
instruments.summary: Federal strategy adopted 15 November 2018 and updated 2 December 2020, aiming for competitive, human-centric and trustworthy "AI made in Germany"; initial €3bn to 2025, raised to ~€5bn in the 2020 update, which added pandemic, sustainability and health priorities.
instruments.source_title: Die Bundesregierung, Strategie Künstliche Intelligenz — Fortschreibung 2020 (Dec 2020)
instruments.notes: Updated 2 December 2020; initial €3bn to 2025, raised to ~€5bn in the 2020 update.

instruments.title: Denmark — National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: Government strategy (Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Industry, Business and Financial Affairs), March 2019, aiming to make Denmark a front-runner in responsible AI use, with four objectives (ethical human-centric basis, research, business growth, world-class public services) and 24 initiatives.
instruments.notes: Four objectives and 24 initiatives.

instruments.title: Netherlands — Strategic Action Plan for Artificial Intelligence (SAPAI)
instruments.summary: Government of the Netherlands action plan built on three pillars: capitalising on societal/economic opportunities, creating the right conditions (education, research, data, connectivity), and strengthening foundations (public values, human rights, trust and safety).
instruments.source_title: Tweede Kamer, Parliamentary Papers blg-903667 (SAPAI report)
instruments.notes: Three pillars: opportunities, conditions, foundations.

instruments.title: Poland — Policy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Poland from 2020
instruments.summary: Council of Ministers Resolution No. 196 of 28 December 2020 (Monitor Polski 2021, item 23) setting short-, medium- and long-term AI goals across six areas: society, innovative companies, science, education, international cooperation and the public sector.
instruments.notes: Council of Ministers Resolution No. 196 of 28 December 2020.

instruments.title: Ireland — National AI Strategy, "AI – Here for Good"
instruments.summary: Ireland's first national AI strategy, launched 8 July 2021 by the Taoiseach and the Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment; a whole-of-government roadmap for trustworthy, human-centric AI adoption in enterprise and public services, refreshed in November 2024.
instruments.notes: Refreshed in November 2024.

instruments.title: Spain — AESIA created, Royal Decree 729/2023
instruments.summary: Royal Decree 729/2023 of 22 August 2023 approves the statute of the Agencia Española de Supervisión de la Inteligencia Artificial (AESIA), based in A Coruña — the first EU member-state AI supervision agency, later Spain's AI market-surveillance authority and single point of contact. Published in the BOE on 2 September 2023.
instruments.notes: Published in the BOE on 2 September 2023; based in A Coruña; Spain's AI market-surveillance authority and single point of contact.

instruments.title: Spain — Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2024
instruments.summary: Council of Ministers approval on 14 May 2024 of the updated AI strategy (continuing the 2020 ENIA), structured in three axes and eight levers — supercomputing, Spanish/co-official-language models (ALIA), public- and private-sector uptake, and transparent, ethical, humanistic AI — with €1.5bn for 2024–2025.
instruments.notes: Continuing the 2020 ENIA; €1.5bn for 2024–2025.

instruments.title: Italy — AI Law, Legge 23 settembre 2025, n. 132
instruments.summary: Italy's comprehensive national AI law ("Disposizioni e deleghe al Governo in materia di intelligenza artificiale"), the first such law in the EU; it sets a biennial national AI strategy, designates AgID and the National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) as national AI authorities, and adds AI-related criminal offences. Published in Gazzetta Ufficiale No. 223 on 25 September 2025, in force 10 October 2025.
instruments.notes: First comprehensive national AI law in the EU; in force 10 October 2025.

instruments.title: Spain — AI regulatory sandbox, Royal Decree 817/2023
instruments.summary: Royal Decree 817/2023 of 8 November 2023 creates the first EU AI regulatory sandbox, under the AI Act's sandbox provisions, for testing AI systems under regulatory supervision; published in the Boletín Oficial del Estado on 9 November 2023 (No. 268), in force 10 November 2023.
instruments.notes: BOE-A-2023-22767. Pilot: single call December 2024–January 2025; secondary reporting says the pilot concluded 1 July 2026 after supporting 25 organisations and producing 16 guides.

instruments.title: Germany — AI Act implementation act (KI-MIG), Gesetz zur Durchführung der Verordnung (EU) 2024/1689
instruments.summary: Germany's AI Act implementation act, adopted by the Bundestag on 11 June 2026 and promulgated on 22 July 2026 (BGBl. 2026 I Nr. 223), in force 29 July 2026. Article 1 is the KI-MIG (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsförderungsgesetz), making the Federal Network Agency (Bundesnetzagentur) the central market surveillance authority, single point of contact and central complaints body; BaFin covers financial-sector AI, and an independent market surveillance chamber handles certain fundamental-rights-sensitive high-risk systems. The act also requires at least one AI regulatory sandbox and adds national fines of up to €50,000.
instruments.source_title: Springer, 'Enforcing the AI Act at the national level: Germany's KI-MIG as a blueprint?'
instruments.notes: Bundestag adopted 11 June 2026; Bundesrat declined to call the Mediation Committee 10 July 2026; BGBl. 2026 I Nr. 223 (issue of 28 July 2026). The Bundesnetzagentur's own press release of 29 July 2026 confirms entry into force; its direct URL returned 404 when checked on 23 Nov 2026, so the peer-reviewed article is cited as the source for now.

instruments.title: Italy — Legislative Decree 160/2026: police use of AI and AI liability
instruments.summary: Legislative Decree 160 of 9 September 2026, adopted under Law 132/2025, aligns national law with the AI Act on police use of AI systems and on civil and criminal liability: it creates a new Criminal Code offence (Art. 437-bis) for failing to adopt safety and human-oversight measures for high-risk AI (1–5 years' imprisonment) and extends civil and corporate liability (Legislative Decree 231/2001) to AI-related harm. Published in Gazzetta Ufficiale No. 214 on 15 September 2026, in force 30 September 2026.
instruments.notes: Code 26G00179; GU Serie Generale n. 214, 15 September 2026.

instruments.title: Italy — Legislative Decree 179/2026: national AI governance, market surveillance and sanctions
instruments.summary: Legislative Decree 179 of 7 October 2026, adopted under Law 132/2025, sets Italy's national AI governance: AgID as notifying authority, the National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) as market surveillance authority, sectoral authorities, penalties of up to €35m or 7% of turnover for prohibited practices, regulatory sandboxes, AI literacy measures and rules on AI in employment. Published in Gazzetta Ufficiale No. 234 on 8 October 2026, in force 23 October 2026.
instruments.notes: GU No. 234, 8 October 2026.

instruments.title: Commission Guidelines on the implementation of the transparency obligations for certain AI systems under Article 50 AI Act
instruments.summary: Non-binding Commission Guidelines (C(2026) 5054, adopted 20 July 2026) on the AI Act's Article 50 transparency duties — machine-readable marking of AI-generated content, labelling of deepfakes and of AI-generated text on matters of public interest — issued under Art. 96(1)(d). Article 50 applies from 2 August 2026; generative systems placed on the market before that date have until 2 December 2026 to add machine-readable marking under Art. 50(2).
instruments.source_title: European Commission, Digital Strategy: Guidelines on AI transparency obligations
instruments.next_milestone: 2 Dec 2026: Art. 50(2) machine-readable marking due for pre-2 Aug 2026 generative systems

instruments.title: Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content
instruments.summary: Voluntary Code of Practice published 10 June 2026 (press release IP/26/1328) to help providers and deployers demonstrate compliance with Article 50: Section 1 commits providers to marking AI-generated or manipulated content in a machine-readable way (metadata, watermarks, detection tools); Section 2 commits deployers to labelling deepfakes and AI-generated public-interest text. The Commission and the AI Board assessed it as an adequate voluntary compliance tool; about 190 organisations had signed by 31 July 2026.
instruments.source_title: European Commission, Digital Strategy: Code of Practice on marking and labelling AI-generated content
instruments.next_milestone: 2 Dec 2026: Art. 50(2) machine-readable marking due for pre-2 Aug 2026 generative systems
instruments.notes: Published 10 June 2026 (press release IP/26/1328); the 31 July 2026 date sometimes cited is the Commission's announcement that about 190 organisations had signed, not the publication date.

instruments.title: Finland — National AI strategy, 'Finland's Age of Artificial Intelligence'
instruments.issuer: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment (Finland)
instruments.summary: Finland's first national AI strategy, adopted 23 October 2017 by the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment, setting eight key actions to make Finland a leader in applying AI — covering business, public services, skills and the legal environment — and launching the national AI programme continued in the 2019 final report and the AI 4.0 programme.
instruments.source_title: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment (Finland), 'Finland's Age of Artificial Intelligence'
instruments.notes: Direct fetch of the source URL returned 403 (bot-blocked) on 23 Nov 2026; the record was verified via AIPolicyTracker, which cites this official source (verified 26 Sep 2026).

instruments.title: Estonia — National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2019–2021 (Kratt Strategy)
instruments.summary: Estonia's national AI strategy, adopted by the Cabinet in July 2019 on the proposals of an expert group led by the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications and the Government Office, with at least €10m for 2019–2021 to advance AI uptake in the public and private sectors, research and skills, and the legal environment; it underpins the 'Kratt' programme of reusable public-sector AI components and the Bürokratt virtual assistant.
instruments.source_title: European Commission, Interoperable Europe: Digital public services based on open source — Bürokratt
instruments.notes: Adopted at Cabinet meeting on 25 July 2019; a successor strategy covered 2022–2023.

instruments.title: Czechia — National Artificial Intelligence Strategy of the Czech Republic 2030
instruments.summary: Updated national AI strategy approved by the government (Resolution No. 520) on 24 July 2024, building on the 2019 National AI Strategy across seven key areas — research, development and innovation; education and expertise; skills; and AI in industry, services and public administration — to develop the Czech AI ecosystem while addressing the technology's challenges.
instruments.source_title: Ministry of Industry and Trade (Czechia), Artificial Intelligence
instruments.notes: Updates the 2019 National AI Strategy (approved 6 May 2019).

instruments.title: Austria — Artificial Intelligence Mission Austria 2030 (AIM AT 2030)
instruments.summary: Austria's national AI strategy, adopted by the Council of Ministers on 25 August 2021, pursuing three objectives — broad use of AI oriented to the common good and fundamental rights, Austria as a research and innovation location, and competitiveness of the Austrian technology and business location — with 13 fields of action covering trustworthy AI, data, infrastructure, skills, public administration and financing, plus an implementation plan added in 2024.
instruments.source_title: Federal Ministry for Climate Action, Environment, Energy, Mobility, Innovation and Technology (BMK), AIM AT 2030
instruments.notes: Complementary AI implementation plan (KI-Umsetzungsplan 2024) added in 2024.

instruments.title: Portugal — AI Portugal 2030, National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: Portugal's national AI strategy, launched in February 2019 under the INCoDe.2030 initiative and coordinated by the Foundation for Science and Technology (FCT), structured around five pillars — inclusion and education, qualification and specialisation, research and innovation, public administration modernisation, and ethics and safety — to strengthen AI capabilities in the public and private sectors.
instruments.source_title: OECD.AI: AI Portugal 2030 — National Strategy for AI
instruments.notes: Succeeded by the National Artificial Intelligence Agenda 2026–2030 (ANIA), approved by Council of Ministers Resolution 2/2026 of 8 January 2026 — to be verified against the Diário da República text in a later run.

instruments.title: Luxembourg — Artificial Intelligence: a Strategic Vision for Luxembourg
instruments.summary: Luxembourg's national AI strategy, published in May 2019 as part of the Digital Luxembourg programme, setting out a vision of human-centric AI based on an efficient and sustainable data-driven ecosystem, with seven pillars — Luxembourg as a living laboratory for applied AI, data, ethics and privacy, investment and strategic partnerships, AI for the public sector, skills and lifelong learning, and international cooperation.
instruments.source_title: Government of Luxembourg, 'Artificial Intelligence: a Strategic Vision for Luxembourg' (PDF)
instruments.notes: A comprehensive review concluded in May 2025; the 2025 'Accelerating Digital Sovereignty 2030' initiative now integrates AI with data and quantum strategies.

Every compute row has an official source.
Version 0.1: first release with 4 incidents, 9 responses and 17 instruments across the EU and 8 member states. Every row has a source link and a confidence rating.
Fixed NL-P-01 source link: the Rijksoverheid policy-note URL is dead (404), replaced with the official parliamentary publication of the SAPAI report (Tweede Kamer blg-903667). No data changed.

Audit and compliance fixes: Garante rows IT-I-01, IT-R-01, IT-R-02, IT-R-03 now cite the specific releases (not the press-room index); IT-R-02 corrected — the Garante set conditions on 12 Apr 2023 for lifting the ChatGPT limitation, service resumed 28 Apr 2023; FR-R-01 now cites the CNIL sanction decision (SAN-2022-019, via Légifrance) with LINC kept as an additional source; NL-R-01 now cites the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens decision page; EU-P-06, DE-P-01 and FR-P-01 now cite the specific guideline/strategy documents; EU-P-08 corrected to two new Art. 5 prohibitions (ba)–(bb) applicable from 2 Dec 2026. Update 2026-11-23: all 8 backlog items resolved — Toeslagenaffaire (NL-I-02, NL-R-03), Irish DPC Grok training inquiry (IE-R-02), Spain AI sandbox RD 817/2023 (ES-P-03), Germany KI-MIG now in force (DE-P-02), Italy LD 160/2026 and LD 179/2026 (IT-P-02, IT-P-03), Garante Character.AI fine (IT-R-04), Greek HDPA Clearview fine (GR-I-01, GR-R-01), and the Art. 50 marking duty covered by the new Art. 50 Guidelines (EU-P-09) and Transparency Code of Practice (EU-P-10) instead of a standalone row. Also added: Swedish IMY Clearview fine (SE-I-01, SE-R-01), Irish DPC Grok nudification inquiry (IE-R-03), Garante Replika €5m fine (IT-R-05), and national AI strategies for Finland, Estonia, Czechia, Austria, Portugal and Luxembourg (FI-P-01, EE-P-01, CZ-P-01, AT-P-01, PT-P-01, LU-P-01). Added a Back to top button and footer links, and a header link to AI Benar Advisory. Map tiles: accessible names now start with their visible text (code, name, number) for voice-control users, hover tooltips are hidden from screen readers (the label carries the same details), and empty-tile names meet 4.5:1 contrast.

Version 0.3: short forms, organisations and country codes are explained where they first appear (hover, or tap on a phone), with 78 entries including national authorities, gazettes and laws in French, German, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese, Dutch and Swedish. IT means Italy, except on the Compute tab, where it means information technology. The Method tab lists them all. No data changed.

The tracker's name and logo now return to its starting view, and the AI Benar home link leads to the AI Benar home page. Restored two automatic checks that were missing from the repository: the review checklist on each pull request, and the check that the page matches its template.

Sources are now saved to the Internet Archive each week by an automatic workflow, and each source with a saved copy shows an archived copy link. The footer now uses the ASEAN tracker's new name. No data changed.

events.title: Grok image-generation misuse and EU response
events.summary: Image-editing features on Grok, built into X, were used from late December 2025 to create non-consensual sexualised edits of real people, including minors. The European Commission opened DSA proceedings on 26 January 2026.
events.caution: The onset date is the start of a documented analysis window of mass misuse; sources differ on the exact start, so day counts are approximate.
events.regional_note: EU-level action: the Commission's DSA proceedings (IP/26/203) opened 26 January 2026; the Irish DPC had already concluded separate Grok training proceedings in September 2024.
